newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS Q1 profit and cash flow up considerably.
newsitem.headline: UBS Q1 profit and cash flow up considerably.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said on Friday it posted excellent operating results in the first quarter of 1997 with group profit and cash flow rising strongly from the year-earlier period.

"The successful start to 1997 bodes well for the rest of the year. The figures for the first quarter cannot simply be extrapolated for the rest of the year, however, since the impact of the markets on business is very difficult to predict," it said in a statement.

"At the end of March, both group profit and cash flow were up considerably on the first quarter of last year, which likewise produced strong results," it said without giving any absolute figures or comparisons.
It said excellent market conditions bolstered earnings significantly in the period.
Lending risks showed divergent trends in the first quarter.

"While practically no new provisions were necessary on the healthy part of the Swiss loan portfolio, provisioning requirements for the weak part remained high. These provisions are charged to the extraordinary provision created last year."

All three major segements contributed to the good operating result, it said, adding fee and commission income posted a particularly strong increase. Earnings from asset management recorded an above-average rise.
Underwriting and corporate finance continued its positive trend, while trading income posted another substantial increase. "No significant changes were registered in interest income."
UBS said the positive trend fuelled higher personnel costs as a result of its performance and profit-related remuneration system. General administration expense developed as expected.
